title: Study: Most US Teens Do Not Drink, Smoke
speaker: VOA Learning English

sentences.en: Drug use among teenagers has continued to drop since the early years of the COVID-19 pandemic, a large national study says.
sentences.zh: 一项全国性的大型研究指出,自COVID-19流行病早期以来,青少年的吸毒率持续下降。

sentences.en: The federally financed Monitoring the Future study has been carried out yearly since 1975.
sentences.zh: 联邦资助的监测未来研究自1975年以来每年都进行。

sentences.en: However, the study only started measuring abstinence – the practice of rejecting alcohol or recreational drug use – in 2017.
sentences.zh: 然而,这项研究直到2017年才开始衡量禁欲,即拒绝酗酒或娱乐性吸毒的做法。

sentences.en: This year’s findings are based on answers from about 24,000 students in grades 8, 10 and 12 in schools across the United States.
sentences.zh: 今年的研究结果是根据美国8年级、10年级和12年级大约24 000名学生的答复得出的。

sentences.en: One major finding: About 66 percent of 12th graders said they had not used alcohol, marijuana, and traditional or electronic cigarettes in the previous 30 days.
sentences.zh: 一项主要发现:大约66%的12年级学生说,他们在过去30天内没有使用过酒精、大麻和传统或电子香烟。

sentences.en: That share, or proportion, of students is the largest since the yearly study started measuring abstinence.
sentences.zh: 自年度研究开始衡量禁欲以来,学生的这一比例或比例是最大的。

sentences.en: The study is “one of the best, if not the best” source of national data for substance use by teens, said Noah Kreski.
sentences.zh: 诺亚·克雷斯基说,这项研究是青少年使用药物的国家数据“最佳、甚至最佳”来源之一。

sentences.en: Kreski is a Columbia University data analyst who has studied teen drug use.
sentences.zh: Kreski是哥伦比亚大学的数据分析师 研究青少年吸毒问题

sentences.en: Among 10th graders, 80 percent said they had not used alcohol, marijuana, cigarettes or e-cigarettes recently, another record.
sentences.zh: 在10年级学生中,80%的人说他们最近没有使用过酒精、大麻、香烟或电子香烟,这是另一个记录。

sentences.en: Among 8th graders, 90 percent did not use any of them, the same as was reported in the previous study.
sentences.zh: 在八年级学生中,90%的人没有使用过任何一种,与上一个研究所报告的情况相同。

sentences.en: The only major increase found was in the use of nicotine pouches, small, white containers of nicotine which users place in their mouths.
sentences.zh: 发现的唯一显著增长是使用尼古丁袋,即用户将尼古丁放在嘴里的小型白色集装箱。

sentences.en: About 6 percent of 12th graders said they had used that form of nicotine in the past year, up from about 3 percent in 2023.
sentences.zh: 大约6%的12年级学生说,他们去年使用过这种尼古丁,比2023年的3%有所增加。

sentences.en: Whether that has the makings of a new public health problem is unclear.
sentences.zh: 这是否造成新的公共卫生问题尚不清楚。

sentences.en: The University of Michigan’s Richard Miech, who leads the study, said: “It’s hard to know if we’re seeing the start of something, or not.” Early in the pandemic, students across the country were told not to go to schools and to avoid parties or other gatherings.
sentences.zh: 领导这项研究的密歇根大学的Richard Miech说 : “ 很难知道我们是否看到某事的开始。 ”在这一流行病发生之初,全国的学生就被告知不要上学和避免聚会或其他聚会。

sentences.en: Alcohol and drug use of all kinds dropped likely because use most often happens in friend group settings.
sentences.zh: 酗酒和吸毒的各种情况都有可能减少,因为吸毒最常发生在朋友群体中。

sentences.en: Friends often influence each other to use drugs, experts say.
sentences.zh: 专家说,朋友经常影响对方使用毒品。

sentences.en: As lockdowns ended, “I think everyone expected at least a partial rebound ,” Miech said.
sentences.zh: Miech说, 随着封锁的结束, “我想每个人都期望至少是部分反弹。

sentences.en: Even before the pandemic, there were decreases in teen cigarette smoking, drinking and the use of several kinds of drugs.
sentences.zh: 甚至在流行之前,青少年吸烟、酗酒和使用多种毒品的情况就有所减少。

sentences.en: Experts suggested that teens were staying home as opposed to spending time in social settings, in which use of illegal substances is more likely.
sentences.zh: 专家们建议,青少年留在家中,而不是在社会环境中花费时间,因为在社会环境中,使用非法物质的可能性更大。

sentences.en: But marijuana use was not falling before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但是,在流行之前,大麻的使用并没有减少。

sentences.en: And vaping was increasing. It was only during the pandemic that those activities began to decrease also.
sentences.zh: 跳跃在增加,只是在这种流行病期间,这些活动才开始减少。

sentences.en: Some experts wonder if the pandemic lockdowns had a deeper influence.
sentences.zh: 一些专家怀疑,这种流行病的封锁是否具有更深的影响。

sentences.en: Miech noted that a lot of teens who experiment with e-cigarettes or drugs start in the 9th grade, sometimes because older children are doing it.
sentences.zh: Miech指出,许多尝试e-cigarettes或药物的青少年从九年级开始,有时是因为年纪较大的儿童在做。

sentences.en: But the children who were 9th graders during the lockdowns never picked up the activity.
sentences.zh: 但被关禁闭期间的九年级学生 从未接受过这种活动

sentences.en: And they never had the opportunity to turn into negative influencers of their younger classmates, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说,他们从来没有机会成为他们年轻同学的负面影响者。

sentences.en: “The pandemic stopped the cycle of new kids coming in and being recruited to drug use,” Miech said.
sentences.zh: Miech说:「这个大流行病阻止了新生进入并被招募吸毒的循环。

sentences.en: Mental health may also play a part. There were increased reports of depression and anxiety in kids after the pandemic began.
sentences.zh: 心理健康也可以发挥作用,在大流行病开始后,儿童患抑郁症和焦虑症的报告有所增加。

sentences.en: Depression is often linked with substance use, but some people with depression and anxiety are very cautious about experimenting with drugs, said Dr.
sentences.zh: 抑郁症往往与药物使用有关,但有些忧郁和焦虑的人对药物试验非常谨慎,医生说,

sentences.en: Duncan Clark. Clark is a University of Pittsburgh medical doctor who researches substance use in kids.
sentences.zh: Duncan Clark 是匹兹堡大学的医生

sentences.en: “Some teens with anxiety are worried about the effects of substances.
sentences.zh: “一些焦虑的青少年担心物质的影响。

sentences.en: They may also be socially inhibited and have less opportunity to use drugs,” Clark said.
sentences.zh: 他们也可能在社会上受到抑制,使用毒品的机会更少。”

sentences.en: I’m John Russell. Mike Stobbe reported on this story for the Associated Press.
sentences.zh: 我是John Russell, Mike Stobbe为美联社报导此事。

sentences.en: John Russell adapted it for VOA Learning English.
sentences.zh: John Russell改编了它 用于VOA学习英语。
